title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #8

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the word for the tiny parts in a leaf where air goes in and out? (1 mark)
   A. Tiny holes
   B. Roots
   C. Petals
   D. Seeds

2. Which of these animals has an outside skeleton or hard covering and no backbone? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Goat
   C. Tilapia
   D. Crab

3. Which of these animals has a soft body covered by a hard shell? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Ant
   C. Snail
   D. Goat

4. Which of these is the best question to ask first when you sort an animal into vertebrate or invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Is it dangerous?
   B. Is it fast?
   C. Is it big?
   D. Does it have a backbone?

5. What does the gullet do? (1 mark)
   A. Absorbs food into blood
   B. Pushes swallowed food to the stomach
   C. Makes saliva
   D. Stores faeces

6. Which of these is a symptom of an unhealthy digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. Sneezing
   B. A headache only
   C. Stomach ache
   D. Sunburn

7. Which of these describes healthy eating? (1 mark)
   A. Eating only sweets
   B. Never drinking water
   C. Eating fruits, vegetables and whole grains
   D. Eating rotten food

8. Which of these can cause stomach ache? (1 mark)
   A. Eating too fast or germs in dirty food
   B. Washing hands
   C. Brushing teeth
   D. Drinking clean water

9. Which part takes back most of the water from the leftover food? (1 mark)
   A. Large intestine
   B. Stomach
   C. Gullet
   D. Mouth

10. What is digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Making food hot
   B. Throwing away food
   C. Storing food in the stomach for years
   D. Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use

11. Which of these is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Heat
   C. Sound
   D. Light

12. There are 750 ml of milk in a jug. 300 ml is poured out. How much is left? (1 mark)
   A. 1050 ml
   B. 350 ml
   C. 450 ml
   D. 550 ml

13. What is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Anything that has mass and takes up space
   B. Anything that makes sound
   C. Anything that is hot
   D. Anything that shines

14. Which of these statements about matter is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Only liquids have mass
   B. Only solids have mass
   C. Gases have no mass
   D. Solids, liquids and gases all have mass

15. Which of these is true of a gas? (1 mark)
   A. It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
   B. It cannot spread out
   C. It keeps its own shape
   D. It is always visible

16. What does recycle mean? (1 mark)
   A. Burn waste
   B. Throw waste away
   C. Bury waste
   D. Make waste into new things

17. Why is it good to separate waste into different bins? (1 mark)
   A. It makes waste heavier
   B. It makes reusing, recycling and composting easier
   C. It makes waste burn
   D. It makes waste smell

18. What can leak from old batteries and pollute soil and water? (1 mark)
   A. Clean water
   B. Milk
   C. Sweet juice
   D. Harmful chemicals

19. Which item can be reused as a toy wheel? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves
   B. Ash
   C. Banana peel
   D. Bottle tops

20. What is the job of the gutter in rainwater harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Carries water from the roof to a pipe
   B. Heats water
   C. Cleans water
   D. Stores water

21. A leaking pipe wastes 5 litres each day. How much is wasted in 7 days? (1 mark)
   A. 57 litres
   B. 12 litres
   C. 70 litres
   D. 35 litres

22. Who should practise water conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Only adults
   B. Only farmers
   C. Only teachers
   D. Everyone at home and school

23. A hockey stick hits a rolling ball to the left. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Changes shape only
   B. Changes direction
   C. Holds together
   D. Starts motion

24. Which surface gives the least friction? (1 mark)
   A. A wet, oiled tile
   B. A thick carpet
   C. Dry grass
   D. Rough sandpaper

25. Which of these holds a shirt together? (1 mark)
   A. A rolling wheel
   B. Wind
   C. Thread stitches
   D. Oil

26. What happens if there is no friction between your shoes and the ground? (1 mark)
   A. You fly
   B. You walk faster
   C. You stop
   D. You slip

27. Which of these needs friction to work? (1 mark)
   A. A rolling wheel
   B. Sliding on oil
   C. Skating on wet ice
   D. Walking on the ground

28. Which of these materials passes heat quickly? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Wood
   C. Metal
   D. Dry cloth

29. Which instrument measures temperature? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Balance
   C. Measuring jug
   D. Thermometer

30. Why does hot tea cool down? (1 mark)
   A. It gains cold
   B. It gains light
   C. It loses heat to the air and cup
   D. It becomes heavier

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. State two uses of light. (2 marks)

32. Describe how to show that metal passes heat more easily than wood. (3 marks)

33. Explain how drip irrigation and mulching save water. (4 marks)

34. Explain the difference between heat and temperature. (4 marks)

35. Name the three states of matter and give one example of each. (2 marks)

36. State two jobs of the mouth in digestion. (2 marks)

37. Describe how a poster can teach the community about water conservation. Give four features. (4 marks)

38. Explain why we should reduce friction in machines and how it can be done. (5 marks)

39. Why should we use LED and solar lamps instead of paraffin lamps? Give two reasons. (4 marks)

40. Explain how farmers use light to discourage pests and animals. (4 marks)

41. Give three safety measures to observe when cooking. (3 marks)

42. Give two ways in which water is wasted at school. (2 marks)

43. Give two natural and two artificial sources of light. (2 marks)

44. Name four safety measures to observe in a kitchen and give a reason for each. (4 marks)

45. Why should you not touch a hot object to find out how hot it is? What should you use? (3 marks)

46. Convert 3 litres into millilitres. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Tiny holes
   Air moves in and out of leaves through tiny holes.

2. D — Crab
   A crab has a hard outer shell and no backbone.

3. C — Snail
   A snail has a soft body with a shell on its back.

4. D — Does it have a backbone?
   The backbone decides the group.

5. B — Pushes swallowed food to the stomach
   The gullet squeezes food down.

6. C — Stomach ache
   Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation are digestive symptoms.

7. C — Eating fruits, vegetables and whole grains
   Healthy eating includes fibre and a variety of foods.

8. A — Eating too fast or germs in dirty food
   Fast eating and dirty food can cause stomach pain.

9. A — Large intestine
   The large intestine takes back water.

10. D — Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use
   Digestion breaks food into tiny parts that can pass into the blood.

11. A — Water
   Water has mass and takes up space. Light, sound and heat are not matter.

12. C — 450 ml
   750 - 300 = 450 ml.

13. A — Anything that has mass and takes up space
   Matter has mass and occupies space.

14. D — Solids, liquids and gases all have mass
   All matter has mass, whatever its state.

15. A — It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
   A gas spreads to fill the space.

16. D — Make waste into new things
   Recycling makes new things from old materials.

17. B — It makes reusing, recycling and composting easier
   Sorting helps each type be managed properly.

18. D — Harmful chemicals
   Old batteries have harmful chemicals.

19. D — Bottle tops
   Bottle tops make good wheels for toys.

20. A — Carries water from the roof to a pipe
   Gutters catch water as it runs off the roof.

21. D — 35 litres
   5 x 7 = 35 litres.

22. D — Everyone at home and school
   Everyone shares water and should save it.

23. B — Changes direction
   The direction of the ball changes.

24. A — A wet, oiled tile
   Oil and smoothness reduce friction.

25. C — Thread stitches
   Stitches hold cloth pieces together.

26. D — You slip
   Without friction you cannot grip.

27. D — Walking on the ground
   Walking needs grip from friction.

28. C — Metal
   Metals pass heat easily.

29. D — Thermometer
   A thermometer shows how hot something is.

30. C — It loses heat to the air and cup
   Heat goes from the tea to the cooler surroundings.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: To see, for safety, to discourage pests, for plants to make food, to dry clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put a metal spoon and a wooden spoon into a cup of warm water. After two minutes touch the top of each. The metal feels warmer so metal passes heat easily.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drip irrigation sends water drop by drop to the roots so little is lost. Mulch covers soil so less water evaporates.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each method.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat is energy that makes things hot. Temperature is how hot something is and it is measured with a thermometer in degrees Celsius.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for heat and 2 marks for temperature.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Solid (stone), liquid (water), gas (air).
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for the three states and 1 mark for correct examples.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Teeth cut and grind food. The tongue moves food and saliva wets it and starts digesting starch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct job.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: A clear message, big pictures, short slogan, bright colours, ideas for saving water, placed where many people see it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four features.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Friction wears out parts, wastes energy and makes machines hot. It is reduced by oiling, smoothing, using rollers or ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for methods.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are safer with less fire risk and less smoke. Solar lamps use free energy and are cheaper to use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: They use bright or flashing lights at night near fields or animal pens to scare wild animals away. Lamps near sheds help to see thieves or pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bright lights, 1 mark for scaring away animals and 2 marks for examples.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use gloves, turn handles inwards, keep children away, do not play with matches, keep paraffin away from fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaving taps running, leaking taps or pipes, using too much water for washing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Natural: sun, stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: bulb, torch, candle, lantern, solar lamp.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct natural and 1 mark for two correct artificial.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Handles inwards to avoid knocking pots, gloves to avoid burns, children away to avoid accidents, switch off iron to avoid fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with reason.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can burn your skin. Use a thermometer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for burns, 1 mark for using a thermometer, 1 mark for reason it is safe.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3000 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer.
